svg.title: SNES saves, bottom net
svg.text: SNES saves, bottom net: a body box, plus an area for each save frame
To scale, the bottom net, the goalie facing up, with the game's own pictures (NHL94_Classic). Stopped: anything in the box, at any height,
or a puck inside the save frame's circle within its height band. Ratings don't change any of it.
Blue square: the body box (11 to his left and below, 10 to his right and above, on the screen), at any height. It never changes.
Green: the save frame's area. It only exists while that frame shows, and only for pucks in its height band.
The computer goalie picks a save move as a shot comes (high / low, near / far). A person's goalie makes one while A is held.
So on the SNES a save move does make the goalie bigger, unlike the Genesis. A diving goalie lets pucks 5 or higher through.
Facing up, the same moves use other frames, so their areas sit elsewhere than at the top net (the stick save's is small and in front of him).
